asr.full_text: When it comes to selecting a new computer, you'll find you have more options available now than ever before. This beginner's guide is designed to help you determine which might work best for your needs and why. Starting with the most basic style, the Chromebook. These run Chrome OS, Google's own operating system. Their primary function is online usage. They tend to be thinner, smaller, and lighter for the price and come in screen sizes down to 11 inches. Now within the Chromebook category there are also Pixel Books. These are going to have the power of a traditional Windows computer but still use the Chrome interface. Chromebooks and Pixel Books are ideal if most of your activities performed with a browser or through apps like you find on a smartphone. They're great for checking emails, streaming videos, social media and browsing the web. Next are laptops or Notebooks, as they're sometimes called. Traditional laptops function similarly to a desktop computer. You'll have the option of Windows or Apple for your operating system. They're available in screen sizes ranging anywhere from 13"-17". They are a portable option that can provide great performance, and with the addition of docks and external monitors, they can be setup in a very similar feel to a desktop if you choose. Laptops are a good solution for someone who needs the portability of a Chromebook but requires more power and a traditional operating system Then you have desktop computers. Those work off the same operating systems as laptops but are larger in size and can accommodate more powerful processors. They typically come with a full-sized keyboard including a number pad and a mouse. They also offer the most flexibility as far as configurations go. Most components in a desktop computer are easily removable making it easier to upgrade, and since their cases are usually much bigger they're also easier to work with when you're doing any kind of upgrading. They're available to accommodate any type of usage as long as you don't need it to be portable, and can be found at a variety of different price points. Another type of desktop computer is an all-in-one. These are kind of like the laptop version of a desktop computer. They're more compact than a full desktop, but they're similar to a laptop in that everything is built in to a compact area and your options to upgrade are a little bit limited. Last, are gaming computers. These can be found in either a laptop or desktop configuration and are all about graphics processing. Gaming computers will have a larger graphics card than a traditional desktop or laptop. This has lots of benefits including the ability to hook up multiple monitors, display a higher resolution, etc. Great for gamers, graphic designers, or professionals who require more power out of their computers like CAD designers, architect and traders. If you still have questions on what type of computer might suit you the best, remember you can always call, email or chat with one of our experts online. We're always happy to help. Thanks for watching and we'll see you in the next one!
